newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bombing toll rises in Algeria. [CORRECTED 16:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bombing toll rises in Algeria. [CORRECTED 16:25 GMT]

text.p: Nearly two weeks of bombings and raids on villages by Islamist guerrillas in Algeria have killed at least 160 people and wounded more than 200, Algerian newspapers said on Thursday.
(Corrects to say toll includes raids on villages)
In the latest reported attacks, eight people died and 10 were wounded on Wednesday when a bomb exploded in a market in the garrison town of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.

A car bomb also killed seven and wounded scores the same day at Quatre Chemins hamlet near Boufarik, 30 km (20 miles) south of Algiers, where 14 people were killed four days ago in another explosion, Algerian Liberte newspaper said.
"Algiers's residents experienced a state of horror and they became scared by any suspect movement around them in the streets," said the Arab-language daily Al Khabar.
No one has claimed responsibility for the bombing campaign since the start of the holy Moslem month of Ramadan began on January 10.
But analysts say the bombs are a message to President Liamine Zeroual that Islamic fundamentalists remain a formidable force despite repeated claims the government has crushed them.

Algeria's radical Armed Islamic Group (GIA) had promised to intensify its "holy war" during Ramadan, threatening a 50-bomb campaign. Besides bombs that killed, at least 17 have been defused in the past three weeks.

Some Algiers residents said their crowded city of nearly four million was experiencing the worst wave of bombings since the Ramadan 1962, when hardline French colonialists unleashed a campaign of violence to oppose Algeria's independence. Algeria won independence in July 1962.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since 1992 when authorities cancelled a general election that Islamists were poised to win.
